titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 7/2010 (ދިވެހިރާއްޖޭގެ އިދާރީ ދާއިރާތައް ލާމަރުކަޒީ އުޞޫލުން ހިންގުމުގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް ... ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This government bill amends the Decentralization Act (Act no. 7/2010). Wherever the Act now requires island and city councils to make a "land use plan", the bill replaces it with a "physical development plan" drawn up and approved under a separate law, the Spatial Planning Bill. Councils would still write their own development plans with public participation and use, lease and invest in council land, but in line with the approved physical development plan. The bill also rewrites Article 107-2, removing the Act's own 3-month deadline, automatic approval rule and list of required map contents, and leaving those details to the planning law. It would take effect on the same date as the Spatial Planning Act.
whyItMatters: How island and city land is zoned and handed out, including where powerhouses and water or sewerage plants go, would follow plans made under the new planning law instead of the council land use plans in the Decentralization Act.
keyProvisions: Articles 1 to 7 amend Articles 22(b), 22(e), 22(g), 23(a)(11), 39(k), 39(hs) and 40(a)(11): councils must prepare a physical development plan under the relevant law and send it to the government for approval, and must acquire, lease and allocate land and register land and buildings in line with that plan.

Article 8 amends Article 56-2(b) so that island or city land is used according to the council's development plan and its physical development plan approved under the relevant law; Article 9 deletes Article 56-2(lh), which tied land use plan approval to Article 107-2.

Article 10 amends Article 56-2(l): each council must publish in the government gazette a register of its leased land, vacant land and land available for different uses under the physical development plan.

Article 11 amends Article 69-3(a) so powerhouses, water plants, sewerage plants and similar public-service facilities must be placed where the physical development plan allows; Article 12 requires councils to consult residents on both plans (Article 107-1(a)).

Article 13 rewrites Article 107-2: after each new council takes office, it must prepare a physical development plan within a period set by the relevant law; once approved, the plans take effect only after residents approve them at a public meeting, and the same applies to any change. Councils approve their development plans and implement their physical development plans.

Article 14 adds a definition to Article 152: a physical development plan means the Island Development Master Plan of an inhabited island or the City Development Master Plan of a city, made under the Spatial Planning Act. Article 15 says the amendments start when that Act takes effect.
whoIsAffected: Island and city councils, the government office that approves plans, and residents whose land, leases and local facilities depend on those plans.
statedReasons: The government says the changes are needed because the Spatial Planning Bill will make the land use plan part of a physical development plan under that law, so the Decentralization Act must be brought into line with it.
